points.text: an edgeless document is the same document as in page mode, made of the same blocks: switching modes converts nothing, and the same doc can be attached to a page editor or an edgeless editor
points.check: Doc: blocksuite/docs-site/components/editors/edgeless-data-structure.md L5 ('documents in edgeless mode are isomorphic to those in page mode. Edgeless documents are also composed of blocks, with no data conversion occurring during mode switching'); edgeless-editor.md L23 ('you can dynamically attach the same doc object to different instances of the page editor and edgeless editor'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): blocksuite/affine/shared/src/utils/model/doc.ts L17-31 (one store per doc with root, surface, note and paragraph, whatever the mode); blocksuite/affine/shared/src/services/doc-mode-service.ts (the mode is a setting, not a format).
points.note: Doc: blocksuite/docs-site/components/editors/edgeless-data-structure.md L5 (isomorphic, composed of blocks, no data conversion on mode switching); edgeless-editor.md L23 (the same doc object attached to page and edgeless editors). In scope.

Documents compatible with both edgeless and page modes have a default surface block as the first child of the root block'); surface-block.md L3-5; edgeless-editor.md L37. Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): blocksuite/affine/blocks/surface/src/surface-model.ts L15-34 (flavour 'affine:surface', role 'hub', parent ['@root']); blocksuite/affine/shared/src/utils/model/doc.ts L17-24 (the surface is added to the root before the note).
points.note: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L28-40 (surface block as the container for whiteboard graphical content; default surface block as the first child of the root block); surface-block.md L3-5. Code: blocksuite/affine/blocks/surface/src/surface-model.ts L15-23 (flavour 'affine:surface', role 'hub', parent ['@root']); doc.ts L24-31 (the surface is added to the root before the note). points.text: shapes, brush strokes, connectors and other drawings are not blocks but surface elements (such as `ShapeElement`, `BrushElement` and `ConnectorElement`), kept in the surface block's `elements` field and drawn on an HTML5 canvas
points.check: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L42-45 ('Graphical content like brushstrokes and polygons are modeled as `SurfaceElement`s and stored in the `block.elements` field. Common element types include `BrushElement`, `ShapeElement`, and `ConnectorElement`'); edgeless-editor.md L10 ('`CanvasElement` rendered to HTML5 canvas, including shapes, brushes, connectors, and text'); surface-block.md L6. Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): blocksuite/affine/blocks/surface/src/surface-model.ts L17-19 (`elements: internalPrimitives.Boxed(new Y.Map())`); blocksuite/framework/std/src/gfx/model/surface/surface-model.ts L34 (`elements: Boxed<Y.Map<Y.Map<unknown>>>`); blocksuite/affine/model/src/elements/ (brush, connector, group, highlighter, mindmap, shape, text).
points.note: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L42-45 (`SurfaceElement`s in `block.elements`; `BrushElement`, `ShapeElement`, `ConnectorElement`); edgeless-editor.md L10 (rendered to HTML5 canvas); surface-block.md L6. points.text: flowing content (paragraphs, lists, images and so on) sits in note blocks: page mode shows the notes in their order among the root block's children, while in edgeless mode a document can be split into several notes placed separately on the canvas
points.check: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L7-26 (one note block by default; 'In the edgeless editor, you can easily split the document into multiple note cards, which can be positioned separately on the edgeless canvas'); note-block.md L3-7 ('In the page editor, the display order of notes is determined by the arrangement order of the note block in the root block `children`'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): blocksuite/affine/model/src/blocks/note/note-model.ts L56 (flavour 'affine:note').
points.note: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L7-26 (one note block by default; split into several note cards positioned separately); note-block.md L3-7 (page editor order = order of note blocks in the root's `children`). Code: blocksuite/affine/model/src/blocks/note/note-model.ts L56 (flavour 'affine:note'), L77 (parent ['@root']), L78-83 (children '@content' etc.). Nuance, immaterial: page mode skips notes whose displayMode is 'edgeless' (note-model.ts L63; blocksuite/affine/model/src/consts/note.ts L38-42; blocksuite/affine/blocks/root/src/page/page-root-block.ts L211, L305), so it shows the doc-visible notes in root order. In scope.

points.text: a block can sit in one of two places: as a direct child of the surface block (edgeless-only, placed anywhere on the canvas, without nesting) or outside it as in page mode (shared with page mode, nestable, laid out inside its note); some types, such as images, can be in either
points.check: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L62-80 ('Blocks used exclusively in the edgeless editor without nesting can be stored as direct children of the surface block. Other blocks are stored outside the surface block, as in rich text mode'; the image example: 'the image with the surface block as its parent can be placed anywhere on the whiteboard, while the images within the note block must be arranged from top to bottom'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): blocksuite/affine/blocks/surface/src/surface-model.ts L24-31 (the surface's children: affine:frame, affine:image, affine:bookmark, affine:attachment, affine:embed-*, affine:edgeless-text).
points.note: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L62-80 (two storage locations: direct children of the surface block for edgeless-only blocks without nesting, or outside it as in rich text mode, reusable and nestable; images in both, the surface one placed anywhere, the note ones laid out top to bottom). Code: surface-model.ts L24-31 (the surface's children: affine:frame, affine:image, affine:bookmark, affine:attachment, affine:embed-*, affine:edgeless-text). 'Laid out inside its note' fits the doc's image example; note blocks themselves also sit outside the surface; immaterial. In scope.

points.text: every note block, every child of the surface block and every surface element has an `xywh` field giving its absolute position and size on the canvas
points.check: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L106-108 ('All indexable blocks and surface elements have an `xywh` field, determining their absolute position on the edgeless canvas'; the indexable blocks are note blocks and all children of the surface block, L86-89); note-block.md L7 ('in the edgeless editor, the position of the note block is determined by the `xywh` field'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): note-model.ts L58 (xywh default), blocksuite/affine/model/src/blocks/frame/frame-model.ts L49 (xywh default).
points.note: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L86-89 (indexable blocks: note blocks and all children of the surface block) and L108 ('All indexable blocks and surface elements have an `xywh` field, determining their absolute position'); note-block.md L7. points.text: stacking order on the canvas comes from an `index` field compared across those blocks and the surface elements, with fractional indexing (as in Figma), not from the order of the block tree
points.check: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L82-91 ('the block tree ... doesn't determine the content hierarchy in the whiteboard'; 'comparing the `index` values of these indexable blocks and elements uniquely determines the edgeless content hierarchy') and L110 ('This hierarchy determination technique is called fractional indexing, also used by Figma'); note-block.md L7 ('its layering with other graphical content is determined by the `index` field'). Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): note-model.ts L60 and frame-model.ts L50 (index 'a0'); blocksuite/framework/std/src/utils/fractional-indexing.ts; blocksuite/framework/std/src/gfx/layer.ts (generateKeyBetween).

points.text: content is associated in two ways: frame blocks, surface-only blocks that mark an area, where moving a frame moves whatever lies inside it by geometry rather than by nesting (and presentation mode steps through frames); and group elements, surface elements that store their children's IDs, take their size from them and can nest
points.check: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L112-117 ('Frame blocks are surface-only blocks with specific `xywh` dimensions. Dragging a frame moves all blocks and elements within its `xywh` area, establishing a dynamic association based on geometric region'; 'Group elements are special surface elements without inherent dimensions, determined by their children. Groups store the IDs of all child nodes ... groups can nest multiple levels'); frame-block.md L3-7 ('based on the geometric area covered by the frame, not on a nested relationship at the model layer'; 'In presentation mode, the viewport will be moved to focus the frames one after another'); edgeless-editor.md L11-13. Code (author's pointers, for the re-checker): blocksuite/affine/model/src/blocks/frame/frame-model.ts L45 (flavour 'affine:frame'); blocksuite/affine/model/src/elements/group/group.ts L18 (`children: Y.Map<boolean>`) and L70.
points.note: Doc: edgeless-data-structure.md L112-117 (frames: surface-only blocks; dragging moves everything within the frame's xywh area, a geometric association; groups: no inherent size, store children's IDs, can nest); frame-block.md L3-7 (geometric, not nesting at the model layer; presentation mode focuses frames one after another); edgeless-editor.md L11-13. Code: frame-model.ts L45 (flavour 'affine:frame'), L59-60 (parent ['affine:surface'], children []), L52 (presentationIndex); group: blocksuite/affine/model/src/elements/group/group.ts L18 (`children: Y.Map<boolean>`), xywh derived from children (framework/std/src/gfx/model/surface/element-model.ts L424-435). Mechanism nuance, immaterial: at this commit a frame records its members in a `childElementIds` prop (frame-model.ts L31, L51) and dragging moves those members, but membership is assigned by geometry: an element created at a point inside a frame joins it (blocksuite/affine/blocks/frame/src/frame-manager.ts L261-274), one dropped inside joins and one dropped outside leaves (frame-highlight-manager.ts L59-72), and a resize recomputes members from the area (frame-block.ts L154-165). There is still no block-tree nesting. In scope.
